answer: Each agent holds a signed jade token that encrypts a unique cipher key linking it to a trusted grove of neighboring nodes. When an agent vouches for a newcomer, it appends its token to a Merkle‑style web‑of‑trust; any later detection of a duplicate or malicious identity revokes the token, instantly nullifying all vouchers that referenced it. An attacker must forge dozens of independent jade tokens and repeatedly repurchase trust, raising the cost to exponential computational and staking expenses.
